items.title: Linear and affine Lorentz maps, and the Lorentz group
items.statement: Let (V,eta) be a 4-dimensional Lorentz vector space (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia) with a chosen time orientation C^+ (def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets), and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be the corresponding oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space (def-sr-affine-minkowski-model). (a) A linear Lorentz map is a linear map L: V -> V such that eta(Lv,Lw) = eta(v,w) for all v,w in V. The set of all linear Lorentz maps is denoted O(V,eta). (b) If (e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) is an ordered eta-orthonormal basis of V (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis), eta_0 := diag(-1,1,1,1) is the matrix of eta in it, and M is the matrix of L in that basis (def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map), then L is a linear Lorentz map if and only if M^T eta_0 M = eta_0; every linear Lorentz map is a linear isomorphism, and the condition does not depend on the eta-orthonormal basis used. (c) A linear Lorentz map L is proper if det L = +1 and orthochronous if L(C^+) = C^+; the set of proper orthochronous Lorentz maps is denoted SO^+(V,eta). O(V,eta) is called the (full) Lorentz group of (V,eta) and SO^+(V,eta) the proper orthochronous Lorentz group; that these are groups under composition is proved in lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure. (d) An affine Lorentz map is a map F: A -> A for which there exist p_0 in A and a linear Lorentz map L with F(p_0 + v) = F(p_0) + L v for all v in V; equivalently F(p) = F(p_0) + L(p - p_0) for all p in A, and L is then unique. F is called proper (resp. orthochronous) when L is. If x is the chart of an inertial frame (def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart), then x(F(p)) = M x(p) + b for all p, where M is the matrix of L in the frame's ordered basis and b := x(F(o)) - M x(o) in R^4. (e) In this framework, unless stated otherwise, 'Lorentz transformation' means a proper orthochronous affine Lorentz map; improper or non-orthochronous Lorentz maps are always named explicitly (the B-page counterexample names the parity and time-reversal matrices).
items.strategy: A definition item: it fixes the language of the page and makes no proof claim beyond what lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure establishes (the matrix criterion, invertibility and the group structure, which is listed as justified_by). The well-definedness obligations are: (i) the set O(V,eta) is defined by a property of linear maps on the fixed vector space V, so it is a set; (ii) the matrix criterion in (b) must be stated in an ordered eta-orthonormal basis, whose existence is the cited lemma, and its independence of that choice is part of the proved content; (iii) 'L(C^+) = C^+' is a condition on a map of sets, not a notation for an unproved continuity statement; (iv) the affine definition (d) must distinguish an active map F on the point set A from the coordinate expression in a chart, and must not conflate an affine map with a general chart change; the coordinate expression requires the identification of vectors with coordinate columns and the cited matrix conventions. The exposition may state that the linear part of an affine Lorentz map is recovered as L v = F(p+v) - F(p), independently of p.

items.title: The passive Lorentz boost with parameter beta
items.statement:
Let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame of the model
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), and let
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ be its coordinates, so that a vector is written
$x=x^0e_0+x^1e_1+x^2e_2+x^3e_3$ and the spatial part is the coordinate
column $x_{\mathrm{vec}}=(x^1,x^2,x^3)$ of $\mathbb R^3$ with its standard
Euclidean structure ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

For $\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$, where
$|\boldsymbol\beta|$ is the Euclidean norm, set

$$\gamma(\boldsymbol\beta):=(1-|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)^{-1/2}\ \ge 1,$$

with equality exactly for $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf 0$ and strict inequality
for $\boldsymbol\beta\neq\mathbf 0$; here the power is the rational power
([[def-rational-power]], [[lem-rational-power-laws]]). The **passive Lorentz
boost with parameter $\boldsymbol\beta$** is the linear map
$B(\boldsymbol\beta):V\to V$ ([[def-linear-map]]) defined by its action on
coordinates: for $\boldsymbol\beta\neq\mathbf 0$,

$$x'^0=\gamma\,(x^0-\boldsymbol\beta\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}}),\qquad x'_{\mathrm{vec}}=x_{\mathrm{vec}}+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}\,(\boldsymbol\beta\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}})\,\boldsymbol\beta-\gamma\,\boldsymbol\beta\,x^0,$$

and for $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf 0$, $B(\mathbf 0):=\operatorname{id}_V$.
Here $x'$ denotes the coordinates of $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ applied to the
vector with coordinates $x$, and $\boldsymbol\beta\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}}$ is
the Euclidean scalar product. Equivalently, in the ordered basis
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ the matrix of $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is

$$\begin{pmatrix}\gamma & -\gamma\boldsymbol\beta^{T}\\ -\gamma\boldsymbol\beta & I_3+\dfrac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^{2}}\,\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\beta^{T}\end{pmatrix},$$

that is, $B^0{}_0=\gamma$, $B^0{}_i=B^i{}_0=-\gamma\beta_i$ for
$i=1,2,3$, and
$B^i{}_j=\delta^i{}_j+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}\beta_i\beta_j$
for $i,j=1,2,3$, with the spatial block replaced by
$I_3$ when $\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf 0$. In the $1+1$ case
$\boldsymbol\beta=\beta e_1$ this reads
$x'^0=\gamma(x^0-\beta x^1)$ and $x'^1=\gamma(x^1-\beta x^0)$. The vector
$\boldsymbol\beta$ is called the **boost parameter**; it is dimensionless and
mathematically independent of any unit convention.

**Consistency of the definition.** The displayed formulas assign to every
coordinate pair $(x^0,x_{\mathrm{vec}})$ a pair
$(x'^0,x'_{\mathrm{vec}})$; writing the result as the matrix product above and
using that $\mathbb R^4$ is identified with coordinates through
[[thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis]] (see
[[def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map]]), the map
$v\mapsto E(M(E^{-1}(v)))$ is the unique linear map with that matrix. The case
$\boldsymbol\beta=\mathbf 0$ is declared separately because the expression
$(\gamma-1)/|\boldsymbol\beta|^2$ is undefined there. That the two cases fit
together is the limit computation recorded next.

**The limit as $\boldsymbol\beta\to\mathbf 0$.** For
$\boldsymbol\beta\neq\mathbf 0$ the identity
$\gamma^2-1=|\boldsymbol\beta|^2\gamma^2$ gives

$$\frac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^{2}}=\frac{\gamma^{2}}{\gamma+1}.$$

Since $|\boldsymbol\beta|^2\le3/4$ forces $1\le\gamma\le2$, the bounds
$|\beta_i|\le|\boldsymbol\beta|$ and $|\beta_i\beta_j|\le|\boldsymbol\beta|^2$
(from the Euclidean norm convention, [[def-abs-value]], [[lem-of-abs-value]])
show that $\gamma\to1$ as $\boldsymbol\beta\to\mathbf 0$; here continuity of
the positive-base power at fixed exponent $-1/2$ is
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], with real and rational powers
identified by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]]. Hence
$(\gamma-1)/|\boldsymbol\beta|^2\to1/2$, so
$B^i{}_j=\delta^i{}_j+\frac12\beta_i\beta_j+o(|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)$ and
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)\to I$ entrywise, without a hidden division by zero.
Here $o(|\boldsymbol\beta|^2)$ denotes a remainder whose ratio to
$|\boldsymbol\beta|^2$ tends to $0$ through nonzero parameters: the ratio
of each spatial remainder is bounded by
$|\gamma^2/(\gamma+1)-1/2|\to0$. The time-space entries obey
$|\gamma\beta_i|\le2|\boldsymbol\beta|\to0$, and the time-time entry tends to
$1$ by $\gamma\to1$. The
definition asserts no Lorentz property: that $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper
orthochronous Lorentz map with inverse $B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$ is proved in
[[lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse]], and its collinear
composition law in
[[lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition]]. The physical
reading of $c\boldsymbol\beta$ as a relative velocity is not part of this
definition ([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]).
items.strategy: A definition item, well-defined because the displayed formulas assign to every coordinate pair (x^0,x_vec) a pair (x'^0,x'_vec), and by thm-unique-coordinates-with-respect-to-an-ordered-basis (applied through def-coordinate-column-and-matrix-of-a-linear-map) there is a unique linear map with that matrix, namely x |-> E o M o E^{-1}. The beta = 0 case is declared separately because the matrix expression ((gamma - 1)/|beta|^2) is undefined there; the definition must not silently divide by zero, and the stated limit follows from the explicit rationalization below. This item asserts no Lorentz property: that B(beta) is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map and that B(-beta) is its inverse is the content of lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse, and the composition law is the content of lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition; the physical reading of c beta as a relative velocity is stated only on the physics items of this page, not here. For the gamma boundary, gamma is positive and gamma^2=1/(1−|beta|^2)>=1, with equality exactly when |beta|=0, so gamma>=1 with precisely the asserted equality case. For beta!=0 the identity gamma^2−1=|beta|^2 gamma^2 yields (gamma−1)/|beta|^2=gamma^2/(gamma+1). Continuity of the positive power in [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]] makes gamma tend to1 as beta tends to0, hence that coefficient tends to1/2. Multiplication by beta_i beta_j proves the leading correction and full spatial-block limit: |beta_i beta_j|<=|beta|^2, so [gamma^2/(gamma+1)−1/2]beta_i beta_j=o(|beta|^2). Thus B(beta) tends to the separately declared identity without a hidden division by zero. No physical velocity interpretation is added. Real and rational powers are identified by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]]. The Euclidean norm convention gives $|\beta_i|^2\le\sum_k\beta_k^2=|\beta|^2$, hence $|\beta_i|\le|\beta|$ and $|\beta_i\beta_j|\le|\beta|^2$. In the norm meaning of $\beta\to0$, $|\beta|\to0$. For $|\beta|^2\le3/4$ one has $1\le\gamma\le2$, so $|\gamma\beta_i|\le2|\beta|\to0$; also $\gamma-1=|\beta|^2\gamma^2/(\gamma+1)\to0$. Together with the already proved spatial-block limit these are every matrix entry of $B(\beta)\to I$.

items.title: Spatial rotations of an inertial frame
items.statement: Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame of the model and let S := span(e_1,e_2,e_3) be its spatial three-space with delta the restriction of eta to S (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame); delta is a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form, (e_1,e_2,e_3) is delta-orthonormal, and S = {w in V : eta(e_0,w) = 0}. A spatial rotation of the frame is a linear map R: V -> V such that R(e_0) = e_0, R(S) is contained in S (so that the restriction R|_S is an endomorphism of S; the determinant condition below forces R(S) = S) and delta(Rw,Rz) = delta(w,z) for all w,z in S, and whose restriction R|_S has determinant +1 computed in the ordered basis (e_1,e_2,e_3). Via the delta-orthonormal basis (e_1,e_2,e_3), these maps are exactly the linear maps whose matrix is a 3x3 matrix A with A^T A = I_3 and det A = +1; such matrices form the group SO(3), and the spatial rotations of the frame form a subgroup of the general linear group of V isomorphic to SO(3) (def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator, cor-orthogonal-and-unitary-operators-form-groups-and-have-unit-determinant-modulus). The extension by R(e_0) = e_0 of a spatial rotation is also written R.
items.strategy: A definition item with its well-definedness resting on the published positive-definite orthogonal-operator material already supplied by def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame (positivity of delta on S and the orthonormal basis) and by the cited corollary (orthogonal operators with determinant modulus one form a group; the determinant-one subset is a subgroup). The definition must separate three objects: the geometric spatial three-space S of a named frame, the restriction R|_S which is the actual rotation, and the extension by the identity on the time direction. The determinant is taken with respect to the orientation of S induced by the ordered basis (e_1,e_2,e_3), which the frame definition fixes; a change of frame changes which maps are called spatial rotations. No claim is made here that spatial rotations are Lorentz maps (that is proved in lem-boost-rotation-factorization).

items.title: Lorentz maps are isomorphisms of determinant +-1 that preserve causal character and permute the cones; the Lorentz sets are groups
items.statement:
Let $(V,\eta)$ be a $4$-dimensional Lorentz vector space with a chosen time
orientation $C^+$, and let $L:V\to V$ be a linear map with
$\eta(Lv,Lw)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in V$
([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]). Then:

(i) $L$ is a linear isomorphism of $V$; for every ordered $\eta$-orthonormal
basis the matrix $M$ of $L$ satisfies $M^{T}\eta_0M=\eta_0$ with
$\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and conversely every invertible matrix
$M$ with $M^{T}\eta_0M=\eta_0$ is the matrix of a linear Lorentz map in that
basis.

(ii) $\det L=\pm1$. The composition of two Lorentz maps is a Lorentz map, the
identity is a Lorentz map, and the inverse of a Lorentz map is a Lorentz map;
the sets $SO(V,\eta):=\{L\in O(V,\eta):\det L=1\}$,
$O^{\uparrow}(V,\eta):=\{L\in O(V,\eta):L(C^+)=C^+\}$ and
$SO^{+}(V,\eta)=SO(V,\eta)\cap O^{\uparrow}(V,\eta)$ are subgroups of
$O(V,\eta)$, which itself is a subgroup of the general linear group $GL(V)$.

(iii) $\eta(Lv,Lv)=\eta(v,v)$ for all $v\in V$; hence $L$ preserves the causal
character of every nonzero vector (timelike, null or spacelike) and maps the
set of null vectors onto itself. If $L$ is proper, then the oriented volume
form is preserved:
$\epsilon(Lv_0,\dots,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,\dots,v_3)$ for all
$v_0,\dots,v_3\in V$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]); if
$\det L=-1$ the two sides differ by the sign $-1$.

(iv) $L(C^+)$ is one of the two components $C^+,C^-$ of the timelike set, so
exactly one of $L(C^+)=C^+$ and $L(C^+)=C^-$ holds; $L$ is orthochronous in
the first case and non-orthochronous in the second, and $L(C^+)=C^+$ holds if
and only if $L(C^+)$ is contained in $C^+$.

(v) The affine Lorentz maps of
[[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]] form a group under composition: the
composition and the inverse of affine Lorentz maps are affine Lorentz maps,
and every affine Lorentz map is a bijection of $A$.
items.strategy: Proof plan. (i) If Lv = 0 then eta(v,w) = eta(Lv,Lw) = 0 for every w, so v = 0 by nondegeneracy of eta; hence L is injective and, V being finite-dimensional, an isomorphism. Writing vectors in an eta-orthonormal basis, the identity eta(Lv,Lw) = eta(v,w) becomes v^T M^T eta_0 M w = v^T eta_0 w for all coordinate columns v,w, which by nondegeneracy of the pairing is equivalent to M^T eta_0 M = eta_0; the converse direction defines L by v |-> E(M(E^{-1}(v))) and computes the same identity. (ii) Taking determinants in M^T eta_0 M = eta_0 and using det eta_0 = -1, det(M^T) = det M and thm-determinant-multiplicative gives (det M)^2 = 1, so det L = +-1. Closure of O(V,eta) under composition: eta(LMv,LMw) = eta(Mv,Mw) = eta(v,w). Identity and inverses: eta(L^{-1}v,L^{-1}w) = eta(LL^{-1}v,LL^{-1}w) = eta(v,w), using L(L^{-1}v) = v. The determinant conditions are preserved because det is multiplicative (thm-determinant-multiplicative, cor-determinant-of-an-inverse), and orthochrony is preserved because LM(C^+) = L(C^+) = C^+ and L^{-1}(C^+) = C^+ when L(C^+) = C^+. Being a subgroup of GL(V) uses that GL(V) is a group (cor-general-linear-group-is-a-group) and def-linear-isomorphism-and-invertible-linear-map. (iii) The first identity is the defining property evaluated on (v,v). Since the sign of eta(v,v) is unchanged, the causal class of every nonzero v is unchanged, and null vectors are exactly those nonzero v with eta(v,v) = 0. For the volume form: in the frame's basis write the columns v_j, so epsilon(v_0,...,v_3) = det([v_j]) by def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form; then epsilon(Lv_0,...,Lv_3) = det(M [v_j]) = det(M) det([v_j]) by multiplicativity, which equals epsilon(v_0,...,v_3) when det M = 1. (iv) L(C^+) is the continuous image of the connected set C^+ (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components), hence connected, and it is contained in the timelike set because eta(Lv,Lv) = eta(v,v) < 0; a connected subset of the timelike set lies in one of its two components (def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets, lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components). Since L is a bijection with L^{-1} also Lorentz, L maps the timelike set onto itself, so L(C^+) and L(C^-) are two nonempty components and hence are C^+ and C^- in some order; in particular L(C^+) = C^+ iff L(C^+) is contained in C^+. (v) If F(p) = F(p_0) + L(p - p_0) and G(p) = G(q_0) + M(p - q_0), then (G o F)(p) = G(F(p_0)) + ML(p - p_0) with ML Lorentz by closure; the inverse of F is p |-> p_0 + L^{-1}(p - F(p_0)), affine Lorentz with linear part L^{-1}, and the identity is affine Lorentz with L = id. There is no unproved step: every algebraic statement is a direct substitution, and the only topological input is the two-component structure of the timelike set, supplied by the cited predecessor lemma.

items.title: The passive boost is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map with inverse B(-beta)
items.statement:
Let $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ be the passive boost of [[def-lorentz-boost]] in an
inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$. For every
$\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the following
hold.

(i) $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map:
$\eta(B(\boldsymbol\beta)v,B(\boldsymbol\beta)w)=\eta(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in V$,
$\det B(\boldsymbol\beta)=+1$, and $B(\boldsymbol\beta)(C^+)=C^+$.

(ii) $B(\mathbf 0)$ is the identity, and for every $\boldsymbol\beta$ the image
of the frame vector $e_0$ is
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)e_0=\gamma\,(e_0-\beta_1e_1-\beta_2e_2-\beta_3e_3)$, so
the map $\boldsymbol\beta\mapsto B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is injective and
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ fixes $0_V$; moreover every vector $y$ with
coordinates $(0,y_{\mathrm{vec}})$ and
$\boldsymbol\beta\cdot y_{\mathrm{vec}}=0$ satisfies
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)y=y$.

(iii) $B(-\boldsymbol\beta)B(\boldsymbol\beta)
=B(\boldsymbol\beta)B(-\boldsymbol\beta)=\operatorname{id}_V$; in particular
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is invertible with
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$, and $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ and
$B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$ are inverse bijections of $V$.

(iv) If $u$ is a future timelike unit vector with coordinates
$(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$, so that $\eta(u,u)=-1$, $u^0>0$ and
$|u_{\mathrm{vec}}|<u^0$, then the boost with parameter
$\boldsymbol\beta:=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ satisfies
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)u=e_0$.

(v) If a vector $x$ has $x^0>|x_{\mathrm{vec}}|$, then the first coordinate of
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)x$ is $\gamma\,(x^0-\boldsymbol\beta\cdot x_{\mathrm{vec}})>0$;
if $x^0<-|x_{\mathrm{vec}}|$ then that first coordinate is negative. In
particular $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ maps the future open cone
$\{x:x^0>|x_{\mathrm{vec}}|\}$ into itself.
items.strategy: Proof plan, for beta not equal to 0 (the case beta = 0 is the identity, for which (i)-(v) are immediate). Put b := |beta| and e := beta/b, so (e_0,e) is an eta-orthonormal pair spanning a timelike 2-plane P, and V = P direct-sum P^perp with P^perp := {y : y^0 = 0 and beta . y = 0}, on which eta is positive definite. By construction B(beta) fixes P^perp pointwise (this is (ii)'s last clause) and on P its matrix in the basis (e_0,e) is [[gamma,-gamma b],[-gamma b,gamma]]. (i) For v = (v^0, v_parallel e + v_perp) and w likewise, eta(Bv,Bw) expands into the P-block computed by matrix multiplication, using gamma^2(1 - b^2) = 1 and gamma^2 b^2 + 1 = gamma^2, plus the P^perp-block and the vanishing of the cross terms (P perpendicular to P^perp); this gives eta(Bv,Bw) = eta(v,w). The determinant is the 2x2 determinant gamma^2(1 - b^2) = 1 times the identity on P^perp, hence +1. For the future cone: beta . x <= b|x_vec| < b x^0 whenever x^0 > |x_vec| >= 0, so x^0 - beta . x > x^0(1 - b) > 0; then B(beta)(C^+) is contained in C^+ (it is contained in the future open cone and connected), and since B(beta) is a Lorentz map with inverse B(-beta) (proved next) that also maps C^+ into C^+, one gets B(beta)(C^+) = C^+. The inequality beta . x <= b|x_vec| uses the Cauchy-Schwarz/triangle inequality for the Euclidean form, and (i) then follows from lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure. (ii) Evaluating the defining formulas at the coordinates of e_0 gives (gamma, -gamma beta_1, -gamma beta_2, -gamma beta_3); injectivity follows because the spatial coordinates of B(beta)e_0 determine beta and the time coordinate determines gamma. (iii) On P the two matrices multiply to gamma^2(1 - b^2) times the identity, using gamma^2(1 - b^2) = 1; on P^perp both are the identity. Hence B(-beta)B(beta) = B(beta)B(-beta) = identity. (iv) Since u is future timelike unit, |u_vec|^2 = (u^0)^2 - 1 < (u^0)^2, so |beta| = |u_vec|/u^0 < 1 and B(beta) is defined; substituting x = u into the formulas in the (e_0,e)-frame with e = beta/|beta| gives spatial part zero and first coordinate gamma(u^0 - beta . u) = gamma(u^0 - |u_vec|^2/u^0) = gamma((u^0)^2 - |u_vec|^2)/u^0 = gamma/u^0 = 1, using gamma = (1 - |beta|^2)^(-1/2) and the unit condition. (v) is the inequality computed in (i). Every step is a finite computation from the definition; the cited predecessor lemma supplies the conclusion that B(beta) is Lorentz, proper and orthochronous.

items.title: Collinear boost composition and the relativistic velocity-addition law
items.statement:
Let $S=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be the spatial three-space of a frame
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with its Euclidean structure $\delta$
([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]), and let $e\in S$ be a unit
vector, $\delta(e,e)=1$. Let $\beta_1,\beta_2\in(-1,1)$ be real parameters and
let $B(\beta_1e)$ and $B(\beta_2e)$ be the corresponding passive boosts
([[def-lorentz-boost]]). Then

$$B(\beta_1e)\,B(\beta_2e)=B(\beta e),\qquad \beta:=\frac{\beta_1+\beta_2}{1+\beta_1\beta_2},$$

and $|\beta|<1$. In particular the two collinear boosts commute,
$B(\beta_1e)B(\beta_2e)=B(\beta_2e)B(\beta_1e)$, and

$$B(\beta_1e)\,B(-\beta_2e)=B\!\left(\frac{\beta_1-\beta_2}{1-\beta_1\beta_2}\,e\right).$$

The composed parameter $\beta$ is the displayed rational expression, which
generally differs from $\beta_1+\beta_2$; this algebraic law is conventionally
called velocity addition. In particular,
no composition of two boosts in a common direction leaves the open interval
$(-1,1)$: the composed parameter always satisfies $|\beta|<1$.
items.strategy: Compute the product of the two matrices on the common (e_0,e)-plane: both boosts act as the identity on the common perpendicular P^perp and fix no other direction, so the product is again the identity on P^perp and the 2x2 matrix product [[gamma_1,-gamma_1 beta_1],[-gamma_1 beta_1,gamma_1]] [[gamma_2,-gamma_2 beta_2],[-gamma_2 beta_2,gamma_2]] equals gamma_1 gamma_2 (1 + beta_1 beta_2) [[1, -(beta_1+beta_2)/(1+beta_1 beta_2)], [-(beta_1+beta_2)/(1+beta_1 beta_2), 1]], which is the boost matrix with parameter beta given above and gamma = gamma_1 gamma_2 (1 + beta_1 beta_2). The algebra proving the display uses gamma_i^2 (1 - beta_i^2) = 1 and the rational power laws. To see |beta| < 1: the denominator 1 + beta_1 beta_2 > 0 because |beta_1 beta_2| < 1, and |beta_1 + beta_2| < 1 + beta_1 beta_2 is equivalent to (beta_1 + beta_2)^2 < (1 + beta_1 beta_2)^2, i.e. to (1 - beta_1^2)(1 - beta_2^2) > 0, which holds since |beta_i| < 1. The minus case is the same multiplication with beta_2 replaced by -beta_2 and 1 - beta_1 beta_2 > 0. Since the identity on P^perp and the matrices on P together define the whole map, the computation is complete; no continuity or limiting argument is used.

items.title: Rapidity parametrization of collinear boosts
items.statement:
For $\beta\in(-1,1)$ define
$r(\beta):=\tfrac12\log\!\Bigl(\dfrac{1+\beta}{1-\beta}\Bigr)$, where $\log$ is
the natural logarithm ([[def-natural-logarithm]]); the argument is positive
because $1+\beta>0$ and $1-\beta>0$. Then $r$ is a strictly increasing
bijection of $(-1,1)$ onto $\mathbb R$. Writing
$\sinh(r):=(e^r-e^{-r})/2$, $\cosh(r):=(e^r+e^{-r})/2$ and
$\tanh(r):=\sinh(r)/\cosh(r)$ ([[def-real-exponential-function-and-e]]), one
has $\cosh^2(r)-\sinh^2(r)=1$, where
$e^x:=\exp(x)$ for real $x$,
$\beta=\tanh(r(\beta))$,
$(1-\tanh(r)^2)^{-1/2}=\cosh(r)$, and
$\sinh(r)=\tanh(r)\cosh(r)=\beta\gamma(\beta)$ at $\beta=\tanh(r)$.
Consequently, for every unit spatial vector $e$ the passive boost acts, in the
ordered pair of directions $(e_0,e)$, as the $2\times2$ matrix
$\begin{pmatrix}\cosh r&-\sinh r\\ -\sinh r&\cosh r\end{pmatrix}$ and as the
identity on the perpendicular complement of the plane
$\operatorname{span}(e_0,e)$. Finally, collinear rapidities add: for all
$r,s\in\mathbb R$,
$B(\tanh(r)e)\,B(\tanh(s)e)=B(\tanh(r+s)e)$, consistent with
[[lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition]].
items.strategy: Proof plan. (a) r is strictly increasing on (-1,1): the map beta |-> (1 + beta)/(1 - beta) has positive derivative 2/(1 - beta)^2 and log is strictly increasing (def-natural-logarithm is the inverse of the strictly increasing exp, thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing); the limits are -infinity and +infinity, so r is onto R by the intermediate value property. (b) beta = tanh(r(beta)): let q := e^(2r) = (1 + beta)/(1 - beta), then tanh(r) = (q - 1)/(q + 1) = beta by elementary algebra of the exponential. (c) Setting beta = tanh(r), the identity 1 - tanh^2 r = 1/cosh^2 r follows from cosh^2 r - sinh^2 r = 1 (itself an expansion using the exponential addition formula thm-exponential-addition-formula); since cosh r > 0, (1 - tanh^2 r)^(-1/2) = cosh r, and gamma(tanh r) = cosh r, sinh r = tanh r cosh r. (d) The matrix display is the definition of B(beta) evaluated at beta = tanh r, using gamma = cosh r and gamma beta = sinh r: [[gamma,-gamma beta],[-gamma beta,gamma]] = [[cosh r,-sinh r],[-sinh r,cosh r]]. (e) Finally the composition statement follows either from the matrix product with the addition formulas for sinh and cosh or from the composition lemma together with the addition law of the exponential; the two routes agree. The exponential presentation exp(r N_e) of the same matrix is supplied separately in lem-lorentz-exponential-map-and-rapidity, which depends on this item, so that this item does not presuppose the exponential series for matrices.

items.title: Unique boost-rotation factorization of proper orthochronous Lorentz maps
items.statement:
Let $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), let
$S:=\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be its spatial three-space with
Euclidean form $\delta$ ([[def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame]]),
and let $L:V\to V$ be a proper orthochronous Lorentz map
([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]). Write $u:=Le_0$, with coordinates
$(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$ in the frame, so that $\eta(u,u)=-1$ and $u^0>0$.
Then:

(i) $|u_{\mathrm{vec}}|<u^0$ and the parameter
$\boldsymbol\beta:=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfies
$|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$;

(ii) the linear map $\widehat R:=B(\boldsymbol\beta)L$ satisfies
$\widehat Re_0=e_0$ and $\widehat R(S)=S$, and its restriction $R:S\to S$ preserves $\delta$ and has determinant $+1$ ([[def-spatial-rotation-of-an-inertial-frame]]);
hence $\widehat R$ is the extension $\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ of the unique
map $R:=\widehat R|_S$; this extension is a spatial rotation of the frame and
$L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ is a product of a passive boost and a
spatial rotation;

(iii) conversely, for every $\boldsymbol\beta$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ and
every linear map $R:S\to S$ preserving $\delta$ with $\det R=1$, the extension
$\widehat R(v^0e_0+w):=v^0e_0+Rw$ ($w\in S$), denoted
$\operatorname{diag}(1,R)$ in the frame basis, is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map and
the product $B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz
map;

(iv) the factorization $L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ of (ii) is unique: if
$B(-\boldsymbol\beta_1)\widehat R_1=B(-\boldsymbol\beta_2)\widehat R_2$ with
$|\boldsymbol\beta_i|<1$ and spatial rotations $\widehat R_i$, then
$\boldsymbol\beta_1=\boldsymbol\beta_2$ and $R_1=R_2$;

(v) $L$ is a passive boost, that is $L=B(\boldsymbol\beta')$ for some
$|\boldsymbol\beta'|<1$, if and only if the rotation $R$ in (ii) is the
identity, and then $\boldsymbol\beta'=-\boldsymbol\beta$ with
$\boldsymbol\beta$ the parameter of (i).
items.strategy: Proof plan. (i) From eta(u,u) = -1 one has |u_vec|^2 = (u^0)^2 - 1, and u^0 > 0 because L is orthochronous, so |u_vec| < u^0. (ii) By lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse(iv), B(beta)u = e_0 with beta := u_vec/u^0; since L e_0 = u this gives Rhat e_0 = B(beta) L e_0 = e_0. Rhat is a composition of Lorentz maps, hence Lorentz (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure), and it preserves S = e_0^perp because for w in S, eta(e_0,Rhat w) = eta(Rhat e_0, Rhat w) = eta(e_0,w) = 0. Hence Rhat maps S into S and, being invertible, onto S; on S it preserves delta because delta is the restriction of eta. For the determinant: Rhat has block matrix diag(1, Rhat|_S) in the frame; det Rhat = det(Rhat|_S) and det Rhat = det B(beta) det L = 1, so det(Rhat|_S) = 1, and Rhat|_S is a spatial rotation. The representation Rhat = diag(1,R) and the equation L = B(beta)^{-1}Rhat = B(-beta)Rhat are then immediate. (iii) A spatial rotation Rhat fixes e_0 and preserves delta on S; expanding eta(Rhat v, Rhat w) in components (v^0,w^0 in the time direction and delta on S) gives eta(Rhat v,Rhat w) = eta(v,w), so Rhat is a Lorentz map; det Rhat = det R = 1, so it is proper, and it is orthochronous because it fixes the future timelike vector e_0 (a Lorentz map maps the cone containing e_0 to itself, by lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iv)); products of proper orthochronous Lorentz maps are proper orthochronous by the same lemma. (iv) Apply both sides of B(-beta_1)Rhat_1 = B(-beta_2)Rhat_2 to e_0: B(-beta_i)e_0 = gamma_i(e_0 + beta_i^sharp), and the coordinate columns gamma_1(e_0 + beta_1) = gamma_2(e_0 + beta_2) force gamma_1 = gamma_2 and beta_1 = beta_2 (compare the time and spatial coordinates); then Rhat_1 = Rhat_2 by invertibility of the common boost, hence R_1 = R_2. (v) If L = B(beta'), then u = L e_0 = gamma'(e_0 - beta'), so beta = u_vec/u^0 = -beta' and B(beta) = B(-beta'), giving Rhat = B(beta)B(beta') = identity and R = identity; conversely if R = identity then L = B(-beta). No step uses an unstated classification of Lorentz maps; the proof is the finite computation above plus the cited predecessor items.

items.title: The proper orthochronous Lorentz group: boosts, rotations, unique factorization and invariants
items.statement:
Let $(V,\eta)$ be a $4$-dimensional Lorentz vector space with time orientation
$C^+$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]] is the form;
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]] fixes $C^+$), and let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an inertial frame of the model
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), with spatial three-space $S$ and
Euclidean form $\delta$. Then:

(i) For every $\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with
$|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ the passive boost $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ is a proper
orthochronous Lorentz map with
$B(\boldsymbol\beta)^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$, and for every unit spatial
vector $e\in S$ and all $\beta_1,\beta_2\in(-1,1)$ one has
$B(\beta_1e)B(\beta_2e)=B\bigl(\frac{\beta_1+\beta_2}{1+\beta_1\beta_2}e\bigr)$;
in particular collinear boosts commute. For each fixed unit spatial axis $e$
and scalar $b\in(-1,1)$ the collinear boost $B(be)$ satisfies $b=\tanh(r)$
for a unique scalar **rapidity** $r\in\mathbb R$, and rapidities add for
boosts along that same fixed axis. This signed scalar rapidity statement does
not identify a vector $\boldsymbol\beta\in\mathbb R^3$ with the scalar
$\tanh(r)$.

(ii) $SO^+(V,\eta)$ is a subgroup of $O(V,\eta)$, which is a subgroup of the
general linear group $GL(V)$; every passive boost $B(\boldsymbol\beta)$ and
every spatial rotation of the frame belongs to
$SO^+(V,\eta)$.

(iii) Every $L\in SO^+(V,\eta)$ has a unique factorization
$L=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)\widehat R$ with $|\boldsymbol\beta|<1$ and $\widehat R$
the extension of a spatial rotation of the frame; here
$\boldsymbol\beta=u_{\mathrm{vec}}/u^0$ where $(u^0,u_{\mathrm{vec}})$ are the
coordinates of $u=Le_0$. Consequently every proper orthochronous Lorentz map
is the product of a passive boost and a spatial rotation, in that order, and
$L$ is itself a passive boost if and only if the rotation $\widehat R$ is the
identity.

(iv) Every $L\in SO^+(V,\eta)$ preserves the interval $\eta(v,v)$, the causal
classification of every nonzero vector, the future and past closed cones, the
orientation, and the oriented volume form of the model:
$\epsilon(Lv_0,Lv_1,Lv_2,Lv_3)=\epsilon(v_0,v_1,v_2,v_3)$ for all
$v_0,\dots,v_3\in V$ ([[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]). An arbitrary
element $L$ of $O(V,\eta)$ satisfies $\det L=\pm1$ and either preserves or
interchanges the future and past cones; moreover $\det L=1$ alone does not
force $L(C^+)=C^+$.
items.strategy: Assembly of the page's proved lemmas, with each clause assigned to its supplier. (i) is lem-boost-is-proper-orthochronous-with-inverse plus lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition plus the fixed-axis scalar bijection r |-> tanh r of lem-rapidity-parametrization-of-collinear-boosts. The vector boost claims use vector beta; only B(b e) with a specified unit axis uses signed scalar b and r. (ii) is lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(ii) for the subgroup statements; boosts lie in SO^+(V,eta) by (i), and a spatial rotation Rhat is a Lorentz map fixing the future timelike vector e_0, hence proper of determinant one and orthochronous by lem-boost-rotation-factorization(iii). (iii) is lem-boost-rotation-factorization(ii),(iv),(v). (iv) combines lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iii),(iv) with det-preservation; the final sentence records the failure of the converse of 'proper implies orthochronous' and is witnessed by the B-page counterexample cex-sr-discrete-lorentz-maps-are-not-proper-orthochronous, whose claim is the explicit matrix computation, not an input here. The proof contract must restate the hypotheses (frame fixed, |beta| < 1, L proper orthochronous) and cite each lemma as the whole content of its clause; no clause may be asserted without the corresponding cited result.

items.title: The Lie algebra of the Lorentz group: eta-antisymmetric endomorphisms and the generators M_ab
items.statement:
Let $(V,\eta)$ be a $4$-dimensional Lorentz vector space and let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be an ordered $\eta$-orthonormal basis with
$\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. For a linear map $K:V\to V$
([[def-linear-map]]) with matrix $M$ in this basis, the following are
equivalent:

(a) $\eta(Kv,w)+\eta(v,Kw)=0$ for all $v,w\in V$;
(b) $M^{T}\eta_0+\eta_0M=0$;
(c) $M$ has the block form
$M=\begin{pmatrix}0&u^{T}\\ u&\Omega\end{pmatrix}$ with
$u\in\mathbb R^3$ and $\Omega^{T}=-\Omega$.

The set
$\mathfrak g:=\{K:\eta(Kv,w)+\eta(v,Kw)=0\text{ for all }v,w\}$ is a
$6$-dimensional linear subspace of the space of linear maps $V\to V$. Define
the maps $M_{ab}$ for all $0\le a,b\le3$ by
$(M_{ab})^{\mu}{}_{\nu}=\delta^{\mu}_{a}\eta_{b\nu}
-\delta^{\mu}_{b}\eta_{a\nu}$. Thus $M_{aa}=0$ and $M_{ba}=-M_{ab}$; the six maps with $a<b$ form a basis of
$\mathfrak g$ and satisfy
$[M_{ab},M_{cd}]=\eta_{bc}M_{ad}-\eta_{ac}M_{bd}-\eta_{bd}M_{ac}
+\eta_{ad}M_{bc}$ for all $0\le a,b,c,d\le3$, where
$[K_1,K_2]:=K_1K_2-K_2K_1$ is the commutator. Here a real Lie algebra means a real vector space with a bilinear antisymmetric bracket satisfying $[K_1,[K_2,K_3]]+[K_2,[K_3,K_1]]+[K_3,[K_1,K_2]]=0$. The commutator makes $\mathfrak g$ such an algebra.
If $L:I\to O(V,\eta)$, with $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an open interval containing $0$, is a
$\mathcal C^1$ curve in $O(V,\eta)$ with $L(0)=\operatorname{id}_V$, then its
derivative $K:=L'(0)$ belongs to $\mathfrak g$, and $L(s)=\operatorname{id}_V+sK+o(s)$ as $s\to0$. Here $\mathcal C^1$ means that each matrix entry is continuously differentiable on $I$, $K$ has entries $(L^a{}_b)\prime(0)$, and $o(s)$ denotes a matrix remainder each of whose entries divided by $|s|$ tends to $0$.
items.strategy: Proof plan. (a) <=> (b): writing v,w as coordinate columns, eta(Kv,w) + eta(v,Kw) = v^T M^T eta_0 w + v^T eta_0 M w = v^T(M^T eta_0 + eta_0 M)w, and by nondegeneracy of the standard pairing this bilinear form vanishes for all v,w exactly when the matrix is zero. (b) <=> (c): write M = [[k, u^T],[w, Omega]] with a real k, u,w in R^3 and Omega 3x3; then eta_0 M = [[-k, -u^T],[w, Omega]], so M^T eta_0 + eta_0 M = 0 reads k = 0, w = u and Omega^T = -Omega. Dimension and basis: the space of skew 3x3 matrices has dimension 3 and u ranges over R^3, so g is 6-dimensional; the maps M_0i (i = 1,2,3) correspond to u = e_i, Omega = 0, and the maps M_ij (1 <= i < j <= 3) correspond to u = 0, Omega = e_i e_j^T - e_j e_i^T, so the six maps are linearly independent and span g. The commutator identity is a finite matrix computation: substitute (M_ab)^mu_nu = delta^mu_a eta_{b nu} - delta^mu_b eta_{a nu}, expand the product M_ab M_cd into the four rank-one products delta^mu_a eta_{b nu}-terms, subtract the expression with (a,b) and (c,d) interchanged, and pair matching terms to obtain the four displayed generator terms; the computation is valid for all index positions including repeated indices, and for the diagonal generators one checks separately that the formula gives the correct sign. Finally, if s |-> L(s) is C^1 in O(V,eta) with L(0) = identity, differentiate eta(L(s)v,L(s)w) = eta(v,w) at s = 0: by bilinearity and the product rule this gives eta(L'(0)v,w) + eta(v,L'(0)w) = 0, i.e. K in g; the expansion L(s) = identity + sK + o(s) is the definition of the derivative at 0 in the finite-dimensional space of linear maps.

items.title: The Lorentz exponential: exp(sK) is proper orthochronous, and boosts are exponentials of generators
items.statement:
Let $(V,\eta)$ be a $4$-dimensional Lorentz vector space with a chosen time
orientation $C^+$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]],
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]), fix an inertial frame
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with coordinates $x^a$
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), and give $V$ the Euclidean norm
$\lVert v\rVert:=\lVert E^{-1}(v)\rVert_2$, where $E(u)=\sum_a u^ae_a$ is the coordinate isomorphism. Let
$\mathfrak g$ be the six-dimensional space of $\eta$-antisymmetric
endomorphisms of [[lem-lorentz-lie-algebra-structure]]. Then:

(i) For every $K\in\mathfrak g$ and every $s\in\mathbb R$ the series
$\exp(sK):=\sum_{n\ge0}(sK)^n/n!$ converges absolutely in the operator norm on
the space of linear maps $V\to V$; the map $s\mapsto\exp(sK)$ is of class
$\mathcal C^\infty$ with $\frac{d}{ds}\exp(sK)=K\exp(sK)=\exp(sK)K$,
$\exp(0)=\operatorname{id}_V$, and
$\exp((s+t)K)=\exp(sK)\exp(tK)$ for all $s,t\in\mathbb R$.

(ii) For every $K\in\mathfrak g$ and every $s\in\mathbb R$ the map
$\exp(sK)$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz map; equivalently
$s\mapsto\exp(sK)$ is a $\mathcal C^\infty$ curve in $SO^+(V,\eta)$ with
$\exp(0)=\operatorname{id}_V$. In particular every $K\in\mathfrak g$ arises as
the derivative at $0$ of a curve of proper orthochronous Lorentz maps. No
claim is made that every element of $SO^+(V,\eta)$ is the exponential of an
element of $\mathfrak g$.

(iii) Let $e\in S$ be a unit spatial vector of the frame, $\delta(e,e)=1$, and
write $e=\sum_{i=1}^3\hat e_ie_i$; set
$N_e:=-\sum_{i=1}^3\hat e_iM_{0i}\in\mathfrak g$. Then $N_e$ vanishes on the
$\eta$-orthogonal complement of $\operatorname{span}(e_0,e)$ and acts on that
plane by the matrix
$\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\ -1&0\end{pmatrix}$; and
$\exp(rN_e)=B(\tanh(r)e)$ for every $r\in\mathbb R$. In particular every
passive boost is the exponential of a generator in $\mathfrak g$, and
$\exp(rN_e)\exp(sN_e)=\exp((r+s)N_e)$ for all $r,s\in\mathbb R$.
items.strategy: Proof plan. Make V a Banach space using any norm (cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach); every linear map V -> V is bounded (cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded), so the exponential series converges absolutely with the estimates of lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator, which supplies (i) verbatim (absolute convergence, C^infinity, derivative, and the group law). (ii) If K in g, then exp(sK) satisfies d/ds[exp(sK)^T eta exp(sK)] = exp(sK)^T (K^T eta + eta K) exp(sK) = 0 by (i) and K^T eta + eta K = 0 (in the frame matrix form of lem-lorentz-lie-algebra-structure); since the expression equals eta at s = 0, exp(sK) is a Lorentz map for every s. It is proper: det exp(sK) is continuous in s, takes only the values +-1 because exp(sK) is Lorentz, and equals +1 at s = 0; a continuous function on the interval R with values in {+1,-1} starting at +1 is identically +1. It is orthochronous: for a fixed v in C^+ the curve s |-> exp(sK)v is continuous, its values are timelike by the Lorentz property, and a continuous path in the timelike set that starts in C^+ remains in C^+ because the timelike set has exactly two connected components (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components); taking v = e_0 or any v gives exp(sK)(C^+) contained in C^+, hence equal to C^+ by lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iv). The assertion that K arises as a derivative is immediate from (i). The explicit disclaimer about surjectivity of the exponential is part of the statement and must be retained. (iii) For N_e one computes (N_e)^2 = projection onto span(e_0,e), N_e e_0 = -e, N_e e = -e_0, and N_e = 0 on the perpendicular complement; hence the exponential series splits into cosh(r) times the identity on the plane plus sinh(r) N_e, which is exactly the matrix [[cosh r,-sinh r],[-sinh r,cosh r]] on the plane and the identity on the complement. By lem-rapidity-parametrization-of-collinear-boosts this equals B(tanh(r) e); the last identity is exp((r+s)N_e) = exp(rN_e)exp(sN_e), which follows from the series or from the addition law of the exponential of a single bounded operator.

items.title: C^2 eta-preserving maps of affine Minkowski space are affine Lorentz maps
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski space with its inertial smooth
structure ([[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]]), and let
$F:A\to A$ be a map whose coordinate expression in some (equivalently, every)
inertial chart is of class $C^2$ and which satisfies

$$\eta(dF_pv,dF_pw)=\eta(v,w)\qquad\text{for all }p\in A\text{ and all }v,w\in V,$$

where $dF_p:T_pA\to T_{F(p)}A$ is the total derivative and the tangent spaces
are identified with $V$ by the canonical isomorphism of
[[lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v]]. Then $F$ is an affine
Lorentz map: there exist $p_0\in A$ and a linear Lorentz map $L$ with
$F(p)=F(p_0)+L(p-p_0)$ for all $p\in A$
([[def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group]]). Conversely every affine Lorentz map is
a $C^\infty$ map of $A$ satisfying the same preservation identity.
Consequently the $C^2$ isometries of the affine Minkowski model are exactly its
affine Lorentz maps, and these form a group under composition.
items.strategy: Proof plan, following the differentiation argument. Fix an inertial chart x: A -> R^4 with coordinate functions x^a and write Phi := x o F o x^{-1} for the coordinate expression, a C^2 map from R^4 into R^4. The preservation identity in coordinates is eta_0(partial_j Phi(u), partial_k Phi(u)) = eta_0(e_j,e_k) = eta_{jk} for all u in R^4, a constant right-hand side. Write A_j := partial_j Phi and C_{ijk} := eta_0(partial_i A_j, A_k). Differentiating the identity in the i-th coordinate and using bilinearity of eta_0 gives C_{ijk} + C_{ikj} = 0; Clairaut's theorem (thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials, available since Phi is C^2) gives partial_i A_j = partial_j A_i, i.e. C_{ijk} = C_{jik}. Iterating the two relations shows C_{ijk} = C_{jik} = -C_{jki} = -C_{kji} = C_{kij} = C_{ikj} = -C_{ijk} for distinct i,j,k, hence C_{ijk} = 0; the cases with a repeated index follow from the same two relations (for instance C_{iik} + C_{iki} = 0, C_{iki} = -C_{iik} and C_{kii} = C_{iki} give C_{iik} = 0). Since the vectors A_k(u) form a basis of R^4 (they are the images of the standard basis under the invertible map dPhi_u, invertible because it preserves the nondegenerate form eta_0) and eta_0 is nondegenerate, eta_0(partial_i A_j, A_k) = 0 for all k implies partial_i A_j = 0 for all i,j; thus all second partial derivatives of Phi vanish on R^4. By cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant applied on the segments u + t h (t in [0,1]), each first partial derivative partial_j Phi is constant on R^4; integrating once more along segments gives Phi(u) = L u + b for a fixed 4x4 matrix L and b in R^4. Evaluating the preservation identity at any u gives L^T eta_0 L = eta_0, so the linear map L determined by the same symbol is a Lorentz map by def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group(b), and F(p) = F(p_0) + L(p - p_0) in affine coordinates. The converse is immediate: an affine Lorentz map has constant derivative, equal to a Lorentz map on each tangent space, so the preservation identity holds; the group statement is lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(v). No differentiability beyond C^2 is used and no global topology beyond the affine structure of A enters.

items.title: Inertial charts are related by proper orthochronous affine Lorentz maps, and every such map is a chart transition
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski space and let
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$, $(o';e'_0,e'_1,e'_2,e'_3)$ be two inertial frames with
charts $x$, $x'$ ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]). Let $M$ be the
change-of-basis matrix defined by $e'_a=\sum_bM^b_ae_b$. Then:

(i) $M$ is the matrix, in the ordered basis $(e_0,\dots,e_3)$, of a linear
Lorentz map $L:V\to V$, that is $L(e_a)=e'_a$ for all $a$; $M$ is proper and
orthochronous: $M^{T}\eta_0M=\eta_0$, $\det M=+1$, and $M$ maps the future cone
onto the future cone. The same holds for $M^{-1}$, the matrix of $L^{-1}$.

(ii) The chart transition
$x'\circ x^{-1}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R^4$ is the affine map
$u\mapsto M^{-1}(u-x(o'))$, whose linear part $M^{-1}$ is a proper
orthochronous Lorentz matrix; consequently it preserves the quadratic form
$q(u):=\eta_0(u,u)=-(u^0)^2+|u_{\mathrm{vec}}|^2$ of coordinate differences,
and it maps future causal coordinate vectors to future causal coordinate
vectors.

(iii) Conversely, for every proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map
$L:V\to V$ and every point $c\in A$, the tuple
$(c;Le_0,Le_1,Le_2,Le_3)$ is an inertial frame, and for its chart $x_L$ one has
Put $M_L:=E^{-1}\circ L\circ E:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R^4$, where $E(u)=\sum_a u^ae_a$. Then $x_L(p)=M_L^{-1}(x(p)-x(c))$ for all $p\in A$. Hence the transitions from the
chart $x$ are exactly the affine maps $u\mapsto M_L^{-1}(u-x(c))$ with $L$
ranging over the proper orthochronous linear Lorentz maps and $c$ over $A$,
and the linear parts of transitions are exactly the proper orthochronous
Lorentz matrices and their inverses.
items.strategy: Proof plan. (i) Since both ordered bases are eta-orthonormal and positively oriented with future first vector, the linear map L with L(e_a) = e'_a satisfies eta(L e_a, L e_b) = eta(e'_a,e'_b) = eta_ab, so L is a Lorentz map by def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group(a) and its matrix is M; det M = +1 because both bases represent the same orientation, and L(C^+) = C^+ because L e_0 = e'_0 lies in C^+ and a Lorentz map permutes the two components (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iv)); alternatively both facts follow from the component structure. The inverse is a Lorentz map of the same type by lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(ii). (ii) The formula x'(p) = M^{-1}(x(p) - x(o')) is exactly the transition identity recorded in def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart; it is affine with linear part M^{-1}, which is proper orthochronous by (i). Preservation of q and of the future cone is then the coordinate form of lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iii),(iv) applied to L^{-1} (in coordinates, eta_0(M^{-1}u, M^{-1}u) = eta_0(u,u)). (iii) If L is a proper orthochronous linear Lorentz map, then the images L e_a again form an eta-orthonormal basis (eta(L e_a, L e_b) = eta_ab), with future first vector L e_0 (orthochrony) and positive orientation (det L = +1), so (c; L e_0, L e_1, L e_2, L e_3) is an inertial frame. Its linear isomorphism E_L is E o L, hence its chart is x_L(p) = E_L^{-1}(p - c) = L^{-1}(E^{-1}(p - c)) = L^{-1}(x(p) - x(c)). The final statement combines (ii) and (iii); no classification theorem beyond the definitions is used.

items.title: Interval, cone and orientation invariance across inertial descriptions
items.statement:
Adopt the postulates of the spacetime-primitives page: the oriented
time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ as the spacetime of the
framework with the equations of the specified model covariant under proper
orthochronous affine Lorentz maps, which are the inertial changes of
description ([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]), and the ideal clock and ideal
light assumptions, including that ideal vacuum light rays are the future null
straight lines and that inertial charts use $x^0=ct$
([[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]],
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]). Let $x$ and $x'$ be the
charts of any two inertial frames of the model. Then:

(i) the transition $x'\circ x^{-1}$ is an affine map $u\mapsto\Lambda u+b$
whose linear part $\Lambda$ is a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix; in
particular for all events $p,q$ with coordinate differences
$\Delta=x(q)-x(p)$ and $\Delta'=x'(q)-x'(p)$ one has $\Delta'=\Lambda\Delta$
and $\eta_0(\Delta',\Delta')=\eta_0(\Delta,\Delta)$, where
$\eta_0=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$: the interval computed from the
coordinates of two events does not depend on the inertial chart used;

(ii) the causal classification of the displacement $q-p$ (timelike, null or
spacelike) and, for causal displacements, the relation "$q$ is in the future
of $p$" versus "$q$ is in the past of $p$" are independent of the inertial
chart used to compute them; likewise the sign of the interval
$I(p,q)=\eta(q-p,q-p)$ is chart-independent;

(iii) the class of future null straight lines is preserved by every inertial
transition: if a curve is a future null straight line in one inertial chart,
then its coordinate image in every other inertial chart is again a future null
straight line, and its coordinate speed computed between parameters $\lambda_1<\lambda_2$ as
$|\Delta x_{\mathrm{vec}}|/\Delta t$ equals $c$ in every inertial chart, consistently with
the light clause of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]];

(iv) the orientation and the oriented volume form of the model are invariant
under every inertial transition, and the composition of two inertial
transitions is again an inertial transition; for two transitions whose linear parts are pure boosts
$B(\beta_1e)$ and $B(\beta_2e)$ for the same unit spatial direction $e$
the composed parameter is
$(\beta_1+\beta_2)/(1+\beta_1\beta_2)$.

**Scope and qualification.** This is a conditional statement about the adopted
model with ideal clocks, ideal light rays, flat classical spacetime and no
gravitational or quantum effects. It is not an empirical claim about nature,
it does not derive the postulates from experiment or from verbal symmetry
principles, and it inherits the idealizations of its premises; no measurement,
calibration or statistical inference is asserted.
items.strategy: Conditional deduction from the adopted premises, as follows. By lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz(ii) the transition is affine with proper orthochronous linear part Lambda, which proves (i) once one notes Delta' = Lambda Delta and applies eta_0(Lambda u, Lambda u) = eta_0(u,u) (the defining property of a Lorentz matrix, def-lorentz-map-and-lorentz-group(b)). Clause (ii) restates in coordinates the preservation of causal character and of the future/past cones proved in lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iii),(iv) for the linear map with matrix Lambda; the identification of the model's physical inertial descriptions with the charts of inertial frames is the content of post-sr-inertial-covariance(ii), and that identification is the only physical premise used, together with the definition of the model. Clause (iii) is the coordinate statement that Lambda maps the future null cone onto itself; the statement that ideal vacuum light rays are exactly the future null straight lines and that their coordinate speed is c is adopted in post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light and is not re-derived here; the invariance of the class of such lines is the mathematical content proved by applying the transition map to the parametrized line. Clause (iv) combines the preservation of the oriented volume form (lem-lorentz-map-preserves-metric-and-causal-structure(iii)) and the group property of transitions (lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz(iii)), with the collinear composition law from lem-collinear-boost-composition-and-velocity-addition. The proof must state the scale conventions (x^0 = c t, eta_0 in the chart) and must not silently upgrade the conditional claim to an empirical statement: the postulates are adopted, not proved, and the idealizations travel to the conclusion.

items.title: C^k tensor fields on affine Minkowski space and their inertial components
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski space of
[[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], with its inertial smooth structure
([[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]], [[def-smooth-manifold]]).
Let $\Omega\subseteq A$ be open, let $r,s\in\mathbb N$, and let
$k\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$. Empty $\Omega$ is allowed; it has the unique
empty field of each type.

Write $T^{r,s}(V)$ for the real vector space, under pointwise operations, of
multilinear maps $(V^*)^r\times V^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]],
[[def-algebraic-dual-and-linear-functional]]). Identify $T_pA$ with $V$ by
[[lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v]]. For an inertial frame
$(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ with chart $x$, let $(e^{*a})$ be its dual basis,
defined by $e^{*a}(e_b)=\delta^a_b$
([[def-dual-family-associated-to-a-basis]]). The components of a map
$T:\Omega\to T^{r,s}(V)$ are

$$T^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}(p):=T(p)(e^{*a_1},\dots,e^{*a_r},e_{b_1},\dots,e_{b_s}).$$

A **$\mathcal C^k$ type-$(r,s)$ tensor field on $\Omega$** is such a map for
which each component, regarded as a function of $u=x(p)$ on the open set
$x(\Omega)\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, is of class $C^k$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; for $k=\infty$ all finite
orders are required.

**Finite-dimensional construction and intrinsic regularity.** Put
$N=4^{r+s}\ge1$, with the component array ordered lexicographically. Every
array of $N$ real numbers defines exactly one tensor: expand each input as
$\alpha_i=\sum_a\alpha_i(e_a)e^{*a}$ and
$v_j=\sum_b e^{*b}(v_j)e_b$, then sum the array entries multiplied by
$\prod_i\alpha_i(e_{a_i})\prod_j e^{*b_j}(v_j)$. This is multilinear and
recovers the array by evaluation on the indicated basis inputs; multilinearity
forces the same formula for any tensor. Thus the component map is a linear
isomorphism $T^{r,s}(V)\to\mathbb R^N$. Pulling back the Euclidean norm gives
a norm on this space ([[def-norm-and-normed-space]]), and every norm makes it
Banach by [[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]]. Any two norms
are equivalent by transporting them to $\mathbb R^N$ and applying
[[thm-all-norms-on-rn-are-equivalent]].

A change of inertial frame expresses each new basis and dual-basis vector as
a constant finite linear combination of the old ones; multilinearity therefore
makes the new component array an invertible constant linear transformation of
the old array. The coordinate precomposition is an invertible affine map by
[[lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas]]. Finite linear combinations
and affine precomposition preserve $C^k$: each first derivative follows from
[[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], and successive derivatives repeat
that rule with constant affine coefficients. Applying the inverse transformations
proves the converse. Hence the definition is independent of frame. Continuous
partials give total derivatives by
[[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], and
induction on order gives the equivalent finite-dimensional Banach-space
$C^k$ definition of [[def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces]] for $T\circ x^{-1}$.
The norm equivalence inequalities preserve the derivative remainder limits and
continuity of each iterated derivative, so this formulation is also independent
of norm. No definition of a Banach-space map with manifold domain is presumed.

A type-$(0,0)$ field is a **scalar field**, a $C^k$ real-valued function.
A type-$(1,0)$ field is a **vector field**, with the vector $v$ identified with
$\alpha\mapsto\alpha(v)$: conversely a linear functional $Q$ on $V^*$ has
$v=\sum_aQ(e^{*a})e_a$ and $Q(\alpha)=\alpha(v)$. A type-$(0,1)$ field is a
**covector field**, taking values in $V^*$.
items.strategy: A definition item. Its well-definedness rests on three supplied facts: the tangent spaces of the affine model are canonically identified with V (lem-tangent-space-of-affine-minkowski-space-is-v); the inertial charts form a smooth atlas, so 'C^k as a map on Omega' has a definite meaning (lem-affine-minkowski-charts-form-a-smooth-atlas, def-smooth-manifold, def-c-k-map-between-banach-spaces); and T^{r,s}(V) is a finite-dimensional real vector space carrying a canonical smooth structure, so the regularity of p |-> T(p) is a property of the map, not of a chosen chart. The component formula uses the dual basis of the frame's basis of V and the identification T_pA = V; the definition must state explicitly that components are frame-dependent arrays while T(p) is a frame-independent multilinear map, and that the component functions of a C^k field in an inertial chart are C^k (the converse direction is the component law). The equivalence asserted in the statement is proved through the constant linear transition matrices between two frames and their inverses, which are C^infinity; no derivative of the tensor field itself is used in this definition.

items.title: Transformation of tensor, covector, derivative and current components under affine Lorentz maps
items.statement:
Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be the affine Minkowski space, let $x$ and $x'$ be
inertial charts whose transition is the affine map $x'(p)=\Lambda x(p)+b$ with
linear part $\Lambda$ (a proper orthochronous Lorentz matrix by
[[lem-inertial-chart-transitions-are-affine-lorentz]]), and let
$\Omega\subseteq A$ be an open subset. Fix $\ell\in\mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ and $r,s\in\mathbb N$. Let $J:\Omega\to V$, $k:\Omega\to V^*$ and $T:\Omega\to T^{r,s}(V)$ be a
$\mathcal C^\ell$ vector field, a $\mathcal C^\ell$ covector field and a
$\mathcal C^\ell$ type-$(r,s)$ tensor field on $\Omega$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], with components $J^a$, $k_a$ and
$T^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}$ in the chart $x$, and primed components in
the chart $x'$. Use indices $a,b\in\{0,1,2,3\}$ and $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, summing every repeated upper/lower index. All component identities compare the same event $p$; as coordinate functions their arguments are $u=x(p)$ and $u\prime=x\prime(p)=\Lambda u+b$. Then:

(i) $J'^a=\Lambda^a{}_bJ^b$: a contravariant index gains the factor
$\Lambda^a{}_b$, that is, components transform by multiplication with the
transition matrix;

(ii) $k'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_ak_b$: a covariant index gains the factor
$(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_a$. If $\theta(p)=k_ax^a(p)+\theta_0$ is an affine scalar
function with constant covector $k$ and constant $\theta_0$, then
$\theta(p)=k'_ax'^a(p)+\theta'_0$ with $k'$ as above and
$\theta'_0:=\theta_0-k'_ab^a$, so the phase function is invariant when the
constant term is transformed together with the covector;

(iii) $T'^{a_1\dots a_r}{}_{b_1\dots b_s}
=\Lambda^{a_1}{}_{c_1}\cdots\Lambda^{a_r}{}_{c_r}
(\Lambda^{-1})^{d_1}{}_{b_1}\cdots(\Lambda^{-1})^{d_s}{}_{b_s}
T^{c_1\dots c_r}{}_{d_1\dots d_s}$: every contravariant index gains a factor
$\Lambda$ and every covariant index a factor $\Lambda^{-1}$, and the law is
consistent with the multilinear evaluation of $T(p)$ after substituting the
transformed basis. Every contraction of one contravariant with one covariant
index is invariant, and the metric components satisfy
$\eta'_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$;

(iv) the coordinate partial-derivative operators satisfy
$\partial'_a=(\Lambda^{-1})^b{}_a\partial_b$ when applied to scalar functions
at points where their coordinate representations are totally differentiable.
Consequently, at every event where the component functions of $J$ are totally
differentiable, the divergence is invariant,
$\partial'_aJ'^a=\partial_aJ^a$. These total differentials exist at every
event if $\ell\ge1$; for $\ell=0$ this clause applies only at events where the
specified components are totally differentiable, and does not assert
covariance from the existence of separate partial derivatives alone. For a
$\mathcal C^1$ type-$(2,0)$ field $T$ one has
$\partial'_aT'^{ab}=\Lambda^b{}_c\partial_aT^{ac}$;

(v) alternating covariant tensor fields transform by the covariant law on each
slot; the oriented volume form of the model satisfies
$\epsilon'_{abcd}=\epsilon_{abcd}$, since $\det\Lambda=+1$, whereas a general
Lorentz matrix with $\det=-1$ changes its sign;

(vi) let $J$ be a $\mathcal C^1$ vector field with components
$(J^0,J^1,J^2,J^3)$ in an inertial chart, and write the spatial block as
$J_{\mathrm{cov}}:=(J^1,J^2,J^3)$ and denote by $\partial_i$ the spatial
partial derivatives in the chart. Then the continuity equation
$\partial_aJ^a=0$ is equivalent to
$\partial_0J^0+\sum_i\partial_iJ^i=0$, and under the passive boost with
parameter $\boldsymbol\beta$ ($\Lambda=B(\boldsymbol\beta)$,
$\Lambda^{-1}=B(-\boldsymbol\beta)$) the components transform as
$J'^0=\gamma(J^0-\boldsymbol\beta\cdot J_{\mathrm{cov}})$ and
$J'_{\mathrm{cov}}=J_{\mathrm{cov}}
+\frac{\gamma-1}{|\boldsymbol\beta|^2}(\boldsymbol\beta\cdot J_{\mathrm{cov}})\boldsymbol\beta
-\gamma\boldsymbol\beta J^0$;

(vii) if $U$ is a $\mathcal C^1$ future timelike vector field and $\rho_0$ a
$\mathcal C^1$ scalar field, then $J:=\rho_0U$ is a $\mathcal C^1$ vector field
and its first component is $J^0=\rho_0U^0$. Future timelikeness gives $U^0>0$
in every inertial chart, so one may define the normalized chart direction
$u:=U/U^0$ and the coordinate density $\rho:=J^0$. Then $u^0=1$,
$u^i=U^i/U^0$, $\rho=\rho_0U^0$, and $J=\rho u$ pointwise. The coordinate
density $\rho$ and scalar multiplier $\rho_0$ are different objects:
$\rho=\rho_0$ if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-1)=0$; at points where
$\rho_0\neq0$ equality holds exactly when $U^0=1$. The vector $u$ is a
normalized chart direction; it is not assumed to have unit or four-velocity
normalization. In an $x^0=ct$ convention the associated spatial coordinate
velocity, if interpreted as such, has components $cu^i$; physical
current/density identification requires its own model premise.

**Interpretation boundary.** The identification of a physical charge-current
with a vector field, and of $\rho$ with a measured charge density, is a model
premise of the electromagnetic framework; this item is a statement about the
transformation of components of specified fields and does not by itself assert
that any physical current transforms as a vector.
items.strategy: Proof plan. (i) and (ii) are the definitions of components: for a vector field, J'(p) = sum_a J'^a(p) partial'_a|_p and partial'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a partial_b, so comparing coefficients with J = sum_b J^b partial_b gives J'^a = Lambda^a_b J^b; the covector transform is the dual statement k'_a = (Lambda^{-1})^b_a k_b. The affine phase invariance in (ii) is the displayed substitution k_a x^a = k'_c x'^c - k'_c b^c. (iii) is the multilinear evaluation: writing T(p) on the transformed basis and using the definition of the components, each contravariant slot contributes Lambda and each covariant slot the inverse; the contraction claim follows from (Lambda^{-1})^a_b Lambda^b_c = delta^a_c, and eta'_{ab} = eta_{ab} is the matrix form of the defining Lorentz property of Lambda. (iv) is the chain rule for the transition x' = Lambda x + b: partial'_a = (partial x^c / partial x'^a) partial_c = (Lambda^{-1})^c_a partial_c; substituting into partial'_a J'^a and using (i) gives the invariance of the divergence, and the (2,0) case follows by the same substitution with the two contravariant factors. (v) An alternating covariant field is a covariant tensor field, so the slot-by-slot covariant law applies; for the volume form, which by def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form is the determinant of the coordinate matrix in an oriented frame, the transformation multiplies the determinant by det(Lambda^{-1}) = 1, and by det Lambda = -1 in the improper case. (vi) is the matrix multiplication of the boost matrix with the component vector; (vii) A future timelike vector has positive time component in any oriented inertial chart. Thus U^0 is nonzero and u:=U/U^0 is well-defined, with u^0=1 and u^i=U^i/U^0. Componentwise multiplication gives J^0=rho_0 U^0=:rho and J=rho_0 U=rho_0 U^0(U/U^0)=rho u. Therefore rho−rho_0=rho_0(U^0−1), giving precisely the asserted equality cases, including rho_0=0. C^1 regularity of J follows by the componentwise product rule. The normalized chart direction generally has neither four-velocity norm−c² nor unit norm−1; in x^0=ct a curve tangent proportional to U has dx^i/dt=c U^i/U^0=c u^i. No measured-density or physical-current assertion is inferred from this algebra. The item must not claim that a physical current is a vector field: that adoption belongs to the electromagnetic model, and the final paragraph of the statement records the boundary. All computations are finite algebra and the chain rule for total derivatives.

items.title: Verbal-postulate reconstruction obligations not discharged by this framework
items.statement:
## What is adopted and what this remark is not

This framework adopts the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space
([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]), its inertial frames and inertial charts
([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), and the assertion that inertial
changes of description are governed by that geometry
([[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]). The transformation law derived on this page
is a conditional consequence of that adoption. This remark records the
epistemic status of the starting point; it makes no further physical or
mathematical claim.

## Obligations a reconstruction from verbal postulates would still owe

In particular, the page does **not** claim to derive the model from the verbal
postulates customarily used to motivate special relativity: Einstein's
principle of relativity for mechanics and electrodynamics together with the
constancy of the speed of light in vacuum (as paraphrased in Crowell,
Section 2.4.1), nor from Crowell's postulates P1-P6 (causality, flatness,
homogeneity/isotropy, inertial-frame existence/equivalence, and relativity of time) (Sections
2.1-2.4). A reconstruction from such verbal statements would still owe, at
least, the following open steps.

1. A precise formal statement of homogeneity and isotropy of spacetime as
   symmetry assumptions, including the class of allowed coordinate changes.
2. An existence and modelling assumption that inertial frames exist, and that
   frames in uniform relative motion are related by transformations of
   constant velocity.
3. An operational definition of simultaneity and of the light-signal
   comparison, together with the assumptions needed to turn the light
   postulate into a statement about the quadratic interval.
4. A proof that the admissible coordinate changes form an affine group
   preserving a quadratic form of Lorentzian signature, with the conversion
   constant fixed.
5. A decision about global topology, since flatness alone does not exclude
   quotient spacetimes such as cylinders that admit no global inertial chart.

None of these steps is carried out here, cited as proved, or used as a logical
premise. The framework's adoption of the geometry is a modelling assumption,
and the obligations above are recorded as open work, not as established
mathematical facts. In particular, no item on this page or on its companion
page may treat this remark as a premise establishing the geometry, and no
claim is made that the verbal postulate systems are logically equivalent to
the affine model.
items.strategy: A bookkeeping remark: it fixes the epistemic status of the page's geometric starting point and lists the additional hypotheses a derivation from verbal postulates would require. It carries no proof obligation and no mathematical claim beyond reporting (from the cited source sections) what kinds of assumptions those verbal formulations contain and what they leave open; in particular it must not assert that the verbal postulate systems are logically equivalent to the affine model, and it must not present the obligations as completed. The item is non-derivational by design: its content is a scope statement, and reviewers should check that no downstream item treats it as a premise establishing the geometry.
